insights.insight: Crinkl has confirmed $2.17M in beta GMV across 37,576+ receipts — each one a cryptographically verified purchase event, not a probabilistic inference. For brands paying $5+ CPM to guess at purchase intent, this is the cost basis that needs explaining.

Grocery, dining, department stores, gas/convenience, pharmacy (CVS + Walgreens simultaneously), home improvement (Home Depot + Lowe's simultaneously), and SaaS/digital commerce are all active in the 14-day window — meaning verified receipt data is not confined to a single vertical but spans the full consumer spending map.

Average basket compresses from ~$65 to ~$53 as grocery and dining grow to 49% of 14-day receipt volume — this is category mix shift, not demand softness, and it means the distribution engine is capturing high-frequency, lower-ticket transactions that are historically the hardest to verify at the individual level.

Walmart leads at 370 receipts in the 14-day window, followed by Costco at 178 and Target at 117 — three mass-market retailers that collectively define mainstream American consumer behavior, confirming the network is not skewed toward premium or niche spend.

Intraday accumulation runs at roughly 10–13 receipts per hour during active periods, with a confirmed UTC midnight rolling-window artifact that drops and recovers within 4–18 hours at every observed boundary — the data is consistent enough to model, which is a prerequisite for any audience planning use case.

insights.topic: Digital and SaaS receipts in the verified set
insights.insight: DKIM-verified receipts include Amazon, OpenAI, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, and Suno alongside traditional retail — confirming the protocol captures digital subscription and SaaS purchase events, a segment that cookie-based targeting has never been able to verify at the transaction level.
